sources.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 8: Variance reduction
sources.locator: Complete 48-page Chapter 8 PDF; focused §§8.2 (printed pp. 5–8), 8.4 (pp. 10–14), and 8.9 (pp. 28–32), including equations (8.26)–(8.34) and Algorithm 8.3.

contents.name: Antithetic estimator, equal marginal laws, and pair covariance variance
contents.reason: The pair law and exact covariance comparison are proved locally for a measurable sampler and the stated 2n-independent-draw comparator.

contents.name: Monotone inputs as a sufficient antithetic covariance condition
contents.reason: The local lemma supplies the complete product-coordinate covariance proof rather than importing the source's monotonicity assertion.

contents.name: Fixed scalar control coefficient, unbiasedness, variance, and optimum
contents.reason: The locally proved quadratic minimization covers the scalar formula and the vector normal equations under positive-definite control covariance.

contents.name: Multiple controls and covariance-matrix normal equations after redundant directions are removed
contents.reason: The item states the positive-definite branch and the design's redundant-direction qualification, and completes the square locally.

contents.name: Same-sample fitted coefficient and coefficient-times-control-mean remainder
contents.reason: The carrier proves both root-n factors from the local IID strong law and finite fourth-moment Chebyshev bounds, then multiplies them.

contents.name: Independent pilot coefficient and conditional unbiasedness
contents.reason: The local conditional-expectation proof uses independence and explicitly states an integrability condition for the random coefficient.

contents.name: Stratified estimator unbiasedness and fixed-allocation variance
contents.reason: The finite partition, conditional stratum laws, and independent draws are stated and the weighted mean and variance are derived locally.

contents.name: Proportional allocation and within-versus-between variance comparison
contents.reason: The claim is limited to integer proportional allocation and compares with the ordinary IID sample mean of the same total size.

contents.name: Regression implementation Algorithm 8.3
contents.reason: Its centered plug-in coefficient formula is captured in the theorem; software instructions and the source's standard-error output are outside the approved claim set.

contents.name: Antithetic sample standard-error estimate and CLT confidence interval
contents.reason: BCS-26 specifies unbiasedness and the finite-sample variance comparison only; it does not authorize a CLT or a confidence-interval claim for dependent pairs.

contents.name: Stratified sample-variance estimate and CLT confidence interval
contents.reason: The approved BCS-26 scope asks for estimator expectation, exact variance, and an allocation-specific comparator, not variance estimation or CLT inference.

contents.name: Neyman allocation, unequal stratum costs, and optimal strata
contents.reason: The controlling design requests a fixed allocation formula and says to state the comparator before variance reduction; no optimal allocation or cost claim is added.

contents.name: Post-stratification as a control-variate estimator
contents.reason: The planned stratum design samples independently within every positive-probability stratum; post-stratification with random or empty stratum counts is not part of BCS-26.

contents.name: Ratio and product control estimators
contents.reason: The plan's supported control-variate estimator is the centered fixed-coefficient regression form; nonlinear ratio/product estimators are outside this page's scope.

contents.name: Expected-log-return antithetic portfolio example
contents.reason: The design calls for a monotone antithetic example with a complete local finite calculation; the portfolio model and its numerical simulation are not needed.

contents.name: Stratified compound-Poisson rainfall example
contents.reason: The BCS-26 example plan calls for a within-stratum variance calculation; the compound-Poisson model and simulation are not imported.

contents.name: Arithmetic/geometric Asian-option control example
contents.reason: The approved BCS-26 examples are control-correlation and pilot calculations; this finance-specific model is not needed for the general theorem.

sources.title: Paul Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering, Springer, 2004, Chapter 4: Variance Reduction Techniques
sources.locator: Complete 614-page book PDF; inspected printed pp. 185–186 for §4.1.1, p. 200 for §4.1.3, pp. 205–207 for §4.2, and pp. 217–219 for §4.3.

contents.name: Control variate estimator, unbiasedness, variance quadratic, and optimal scalar coefficient
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the same fixed-coefficient identities and states the finite-moment hypotheses explicitly.

contents.name: Multiple control variates and regression normal equations
contents.reason: The local vector proof gives the normal equations through covariance notation and a positive-definite covariance matrix.

contents.name: Small-sample bias from estimating the coefficient on the production data
contents.reason: The theorem states only the source-supported remainder order; the B-page finite example directly verifies a nonzero bias case.

contents.name: Independent pilot/split sample coefficient removes the dependence responsible for plug-in bias
contents.reason: A conditional expectation argument is supplied locally for an integrable pilot coefficient independent of the production sample.

contents.name: Antithetic estimator as the mean of independent pair averages
contents.reason: The local proof verifies pair independence from IID inputs and allows dependence within each pair.

contents.name: Negative covariance criterion and monotone sufficient condition for antithetics
contents.reason: The comparison uses the same number of function evaluations and the monotone criterion is proved by a local lemma.

contents.name: Stratified estimator and exact variance by stratum
contents.reason: The exact weighted variance is proved for finite measurable partitions and mutually independent conditional draws.

contents.name: Proportional allocation cannot increase variance relative to crude Monte Carlo
contents.reason: The carrier proves this only for integer proportional allocation and explicitly names the ordinary IID comparator.

contents.name: Optimal allocation with equal or unequal computational costs
contents.reason: BCS-26 requires a stated allocation/comparator for its variance claim but does not include a cost-optimization or Neyman-allocation theorem.

contents.name: Finance-specific tractable-dynamics control examples and option-price applications
contents.reason: The pair's planned examples are complete elementary probability calculations; model-specific derivative-pricing assumptions are not needed.

contents.name: Antithetic and stratified confidence intervals and their CLT discussion
contents.reason: The controlling design does not claim a CLT or a standard-error estimator for these dependent or allocated designs.

sources.title: Jonathan Goodman, Lecture Notes on Monte Carlo Methods, NYU, Fall 2007, Chapter 3: Variance Reduction
sources.locator: Complete 12-page PDF; focused Chapter 3 §2, ‘Control variates,’ PDF pp. 1–3, including scalar variance minimization and vector normal equations.

contents.name: Fixed-coefficient control estimator and unbiasedness
contents.reason: The theorem's local proof includes expectation linearity and the centered known-mean control term.

contents.name: Scalar optimal coefficient and minimum variance
contents.reason: The local proof derives the coefficient by completing the variance quadratic, including its variance-zero and covariance-zero cases.

contents.name: Vector controls and covariance normal equations
contents.reason: The vector branch is proved locally under a positive-definite covariance matrix and states how redundant directions are handled.

contents.name: Finite-dimensional unit-ball control-variate numerical illustration
contents.reason: The BCS-26 example plan calls for exact finite or elementary checks, so this simulated six-dimensional illustration is not copied.

contents.name: Rao–Blackwell partial averaging, importance sampling, and asymptotic integration in other lecture sections
contents.reason: Only the lecture's control-variate treatment supports this pair; the other methods belong to separate planned pages and are not imported here.

companions.reason: The six examples are locally calculated consequences and counterexamples using this pair's A-page results; no separate B-page source harvest is claimed.
